title: Predicting Patients Requiring Treatment for Depression in the Postpartum Period Using Common Electronic Medical Record Data Available Antepartum.
summary: The study trains machine-learning models on a prospective NIH pregnancy cohort; among 8,454 births, 338 had postpartum depression. The best model achieved AUC 0.91 and identified prepregnancy depression history as the strongest predictor, with sociodemographic/clinical variables also contributing. This is retrospective prediction within the cohort, not proof of causal risk or intervention benefit.
